Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program Terms of Reference for: Digital Transformation Senior Coordinator Reference No.: JO-MOE-566807-CS-INDV Program Background: The Modernizing Education, Skills, and Administrative Reforms (MASAR) Program for Results (PforR) is a transformative, system-wide reform initiative anchored in Jordan’s Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). The MASAR Operation is designed to support the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development in addressing foundational bottlenecks in access, quality, and relevance of education, with a dual emphasis on equity and efficiency. The operation aims to strengthen institutional capacity while enabling measurable improvements in learning outcomes and employability, particularly through early childhood education and labor market-aligned technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and digital transformation in education. The program became effective in 2024, with a total financing envelope of USD 400 million, supported by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). It comprises two core components: Program-for-Results (PforR) : the principal financing instrument that disburses against verified achievement of results tied to government reform priorities. Investment Project Financing (IPF) : a complementary technical assistance (TA) component aimed at supporting the implementation of system-strengthening activities and accelerating the achievement of Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs). MASAR is structured around four interlinked Results Areas (RAs) that are strategically aligned with key education-sector transition points and cross-cutting governance reforms: RA1: Home to School – Expanding Access to Foundational Learning. This includes (i) increasing equitable access to KG2, particularly in under-served districts and refugee-hosting communities; (ii) enhancing the quality of early childhood education through a revised KG1-KG2 curriculum and quality assurance mechanisms; and (iii) improving foundational literacy skills for Grades 1–3 through targeted pedagogical interventions and a comprehensive implementation plan. RA2: School to Work – Increasing Access to Labor Market-Relevant TVET. MASAR seeks to improve the alignment of TVET with private sector needs by institutionalizing public-private partnerships, scaling apprenticeships, and expanding career guidance and employment pathways. This is complemented by the operationalization of an equivalency system that supports the portability and recognition of TVET qualifications, and enhanced use of learner trajectory data to inform student support services. RA3: Strengthening Sector Governance and Efficiency. The program supports the operationalization of a restructured governance model for the education sector and introduces reforms to human resource management, with a particular focus on teacher recruitment, deployment, and professional development policies. RA4: Digital Transformation in Education, to be introduced through the MASAR Additional Financing (AF), supporting digital and AI-enabled learning for students in Grades 4-12 and strengthening the institutional infrastructure needed for national-scale technology integration in education. In addition to its core education objectives, MASAR embeds environmental and social sustainability principles across its implementation. Ultimately, MASAR is designed to deliver measurable, inclusive, and sustainable improvements in Jordan’s education system. It expands access to early learning, strengthens foundational skills, improves graduate employability, strengthens digital skills, technology-enabled learning, and future-ready competencies, and reinforces institutional coherence through evidence-based policymaking. TED-748747-2026.title: Belgium – Business and management consultancy and related services – Learning through Experimentation for Adaptive Programming (LEAP) - Producing experimental designs for ERDF/CF/JTF investment in the field of energy efficiency measures
TED-748747-2026.description: The overarching goal of this assignment is to prepare the ground for embedding experimentation in National and Regional Partnership Plans from the outset of the 2028–2034 programming period. To this end, the assignment will structurally bring evaluators and programmers to work together, build capacity on both sides, and provide the EU evaluation system with practical experimentation tools that extend beyond the three participating MS. This assignment focuses on investments on energy efficiency measures and shall produce the following outputs: 1. NRPP-ready experimental designs to be implemented in the 2028–2034 programming period in three Member States; 2. a detailed toolkit to support MS in the introduction of experimental designs in 2028-2034 Plans: LEAP Kit (Learning through Experimentation for Adaptive Programming). Energy efficiency is central to the EU’s climate, cohesion, and energy security objectives. Reducing energy consumption across the built environment, industrial processes, district energy networks, and community energy systems contributes directly to cutting greenhouse gas emissions, reducing dependence on imported fossil fuels, and ensuring more resilient and affordable energy supply. All of which are particularly pressing in less developed and transition regions where energy poverty, ageing building stock, and limited private investment capacity make public intervention most necessary. Despite its widespread use, substantial analysis remains to be made in assessing the effectiveness of energy efficiency investments and identifying the conditions under which these generate the expected impact. Experimentation through randomised controlled trials (RCTs) - and the analysis of experiment results to identify the causal effects of interventions - offers the most rigorous way to generate this evidence. Improving the capacity to design and conduct experimental designs is even more important in light of the evolving regulatory context. The Commission proposal for the 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework explicitly promotes policy learning and experimentation as a function of both coordinating and managing authorities (Articles 50 and 51 of the proposed Performance Regulation). DG REGIO’s ambition is that experimental designs and adaptive learning mechanisms will be embedded in the National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs) from the outset of the next programming period.

TED-745428-2026.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have been expanding into new areas of application for years. AI systems are increasingly capable of handling complex tasks with greater autonomy—for example, through agent-based approaches that run an AI agent on a computer to perform any task automatically or even autonomously, sometimes without explicit human instructions but rather based on identified intentions (see, for example, the open-source software OpenClaw, which can handle tasks such as calendar maintenance or file management). Just how deeply AI algorithms and models are now integrated into everyday applications is also evident in the fact that end devices are increasingly operable entirely without visible applications and exclusively via voice control, which fundamentally rethinks the way we interact with them (such as Deutsche Telekom’s AI Phone). The central control units of such end devices—the operating systems themselves—are also increasingly being enhanced with new AI functionalities to continuously improve system efficiency. These include initial theoretical—and in some cases already practical—approaches to using the latest AI technologies for file system or storage management. These developments mark a fundamental paradigm shift: AI is no longer viewed merely as an add-on, but increasingly as a native architectural component of the operating system itself. The AI-as-OS program aims to explore how artificial intelligence can be understood not merely as a separately encapsulated functionality that is simply executed by the operating system, but as the operating system itself—Artificial Intelligence as Operating System. Behind this lies the vision of an AI that not only supports individual applications but also acts as the central control system for the entire computer ecosystem, managing system resources (including the CPU, RAM, and system security) in a data-driven, adaptive, and context-aware manner. The aim of the program is to make fundamental contributions to the development of AI-based operating systems as the control unit of a computer system. Through the extensive integration of AI technologies into deep operating system layers, such a system is intended to manage system resources, enable context-aware operational decisions, and enhance system security through adaptive threat detection and defense. Since the underlying technology is still largely in a speculative stage, the scope of development work ranges from the general architecture of such an operating system to the integration of AI-based core mechanisms, and includes new considerations regarding the security and stability requirements for such an operating system, depending on the target platform (e.g., desktop, data center, edge device) and the application environment. The program’s main areas of research include: • AI-Centric Operating System Architectures: Concepts for the fundamental design of an operating system in which AI is viewed not as an add-on feature but as an integral part of the architecture. • AI-Native Core Mechanisms: Integration of AI-based methods into core operating system functions such as resource management, process control, and memory organization. • Control, Security, and Stability: Requirements for traceability, controllability, and robustness of an AI-based operating system, as well as approaches to adaptive threat detection and defense. From today’s perspective, it remains to be seen whether—and to what extent—the vision of an AI-native operating system can be technically realized. This is precisely where the program’s value lies: AI-as-OS explores a largely speculative field at the intersection of AI research and system software, the results of which could set the course for the operating systems of tomorrow.

TED-757336-2026.title: Poland – Wastewater treatment plant construction work – Przebudowa i rozbudowa istniejącej oczyszczalni ścieków w Nowogardzie
TED-757336-2026.description: 1. Przedmiotem opracowania jest zaprojektowanie i wykonanie inwestycji pn.: „Przebudowa i rozbudowa istniejącej oczyszczalni ścieków w Nowogardzie”. Obecnie funkcjonująca oczyszczalnia ścieków zlokalizowana jest w Nowogardzie, w północno-wschodniej części miejscowości przy ulicy Zamkowej 9. Przedmiot zamówienia obejmuje kompleksową realizację Inwestycji, w szczególności: a) opracowanie kompletnej dokumentacji projektowej, uzyskanie wszelkich niezbędnych decyzji administracyjnych, opinii i uzgodnień wymaganych przepisami prawa, w tym m.in. pozwolenia na budowę oraz (jeśli dotyczy) aktualizacji pozwolenia wodnoprawnego; b) wykonanie wszystkich Robót budowlanych oraz dostaw maszyn i urządzeń zgodnie z zatwierdzoną dokumentacją projektową i PFU; c) sprawowanie nadzoru autorskiego w trakcie realizacji robót budowlanych; d) przeprowadzenie pełnego procesu Rozruchu oraz Ruchu Próbnego (Próby Eksploatacyjnej) wraz z potwierdzeniem osiągnięcia Parametrów Kontrolnych i Efektu Ekologicznego; e) uzyskanie w imieniu Zamawiającego ostatecznej decyzji o pozwoleniu na użytkowanie; f) udzielenie Gwarancji na zasadach określonych w umowie; Obecna mechaniczno-biologiczna oczyszczalnia ścieków w Nowogardzie posiada przepustowość projektową Qśrd= 3 420 m3/d, została wybudowana w latach 1972 – 1975 (Dokumentacja projektowa powstała w 1969r.). W realizacji przedmiotowej inwestycji należy uwzględnić rozbudowę i przebudowę (modernizację) istniejącej oczyszczalni w zakresie oczyszczalni mechanicznej, oczyszczalni biologicznej i gospodarki osadowej na działce istniejącej oczyszczalni Nowogard OBR. 3 – nr 200 o powierzchni 2,5090 ha. Osiągnięcie powyższych założeń związane jest ściśle z rozbudową i przebudową istniejących i wykonaniem nowych obiektów technologicznych na działce nr ew. 200 w konstrukcji żelbetowej z zaawansowanym technicznie wyposażeniem technologicznym oraz systemem AKPiA. Wymaga się automatyzacji procesów technologicznych bazującej na wysokosprawnych urządzeniach pomiarowych oraz zautomatyzowanym systemie sterowania dla optymalizacji procesu oczyszczania i jednoczesnego ograniczenia kosztów, których jednym z najwyższych czynników jest zużycie energii elektrycznej na proces napowietrzania i unieszkodliwianie osadów ściekowych. Analiza danych ilościowo-jakościowych ścieków surowych, stan i parametry techniczne kanalizacji sanitarnej na terenie gminy Nowogard warunkują zakres rozbudowy i przebudowy przedmiotowej oczyszczalni. Projektowane obciążenie oczyszczalni wyrażone Równoważną Liczbą Mieszkańców nie może być niższe od RLM=25920. Dla tej wielkości oczyszczalni, należy spełnić wymagania jakościowe w odprowadzanych ściekach oczyszczonych zawarte w obowiązującym rozporządzeniu Ministra gospodarki morskiej i żeglugi śródlądowej z dnia 12 lipca 2019 w sprawie substancji szczególnie szkodliwych dla środowiska wodnego oraz warunków, jakie należy spełnić przy wprowadzaniu do wód lub do ziemi ścieków, a także przy odprowadzaniu wód opadowych lub roztopowych do wód lub do urządzeń wodnych – Dz. U 2019, poz. 1311. Wymagany efekt ekologiczny należy uzyskać przy zastosowaniu wysokosprawnej oczyszczalni mechanicznej z piaskownikiem poziomym, nowoprojektowanego reaktora biologicznego w technologii A2O. Należy zaprojektować i wykonać gospodarkę osadową z tlenową stabilizacją i dwukierunkową higienizacją: mikrobiologiczną z zastosowaniem efektywnych mikroorganizmów i termiczną z wykorzystaniem Termicznego Higienizatora Osadów (THO). Każdy z wymaganych metod higienizacji musi zapewnić parametry wymagane do stosowania komunalnych osadów ściekowych w rolnictwie.
